Depth substitutes for scarce width by composing features when capacity is limited.
Narrow nets are capacity-limited and extra L2 deepens underfitting.
The L2 term is divided by batch size, so at small batches the same alpha is a much stronger penalty and over-regularizes.
The L2 penalty sums over more weights as width grows, so strong alpha underfits wide nets more.
Small batches already inject noise and many updates, so a higher LR more easily crosses the stability edge.

Strong L2 applies to every layer, so extra layers multiply the shrinkage and attenuate the signal, deepening underfitting.
